Living in Totterdown

Updated 2 November 2026. Every figure links to its source. Prices and ratings change, so check the source before you decide. How we check facts.

Totterdown is a neighbourhood of Victorian terraces on a steep hill in south Bristol, in the BS4 postcode, a short walk from Temple Meads station. This guide covers the practical side of living here.

Quick answer

  • House prices: homes in Totterdown sold for an average of £374,399 over the year to early 2026, 5% more than the year before. [1]
  • Council ward: Totterdown is in Windmill Hill ward, home to an estimated 14,104 people in mid-2024. [2] [3]
  • Getting about: Temple Meads station is at the foot of the hill, within walking distance. [4]
  • Parking: a residents' parking scheme is proposed; the council's survey closes on 5 November 2026. Details
  • Clean Air Zone: Totterdown is outside Bristol's zone, which starts at the Three Lamps junction. [5]

Most homes in Totterdown are terraced houses, so the average reflects a mix of terrace sizes. Check recent sales on your street before making an offer. [1]

Where is Totterdown, and which ward is it in?

  • Location: south of the River Avon, above Temple Meads, where the A4 Bath Road and the A37 Wells Road split at Three Lamps. [6]
  • Ward: since 2016, Totterdown has been part of Windmill Hill ward, with the south-eastern part of Bedminster and the Ravenhill Road area of Lower Knowle. [2]
  • Population: the ward had 13,958 residents at the 2021 Census and an estimated 14,104 in mid-2024. Neither figure is for Totterdown alone. [7] [3]

What schools are in Totterdown?

  • Hillcrest Primary School on Cemetery Road is a community primary school for ages 4 to 11. It was rated Good at its January 2022 inspection. Ofsted now publishes report cards, so check its page for anything newer. [8]
  • Admissions: school places in Bristol are allocated by the city council, so check the council's admissions pages for catchment and deadlines.

How do you get around from Totterdown?

  • Train: Bristol Temple Meads is at the bottom of the hill. Visit Bristol's walking route from the station runs through Totterdown's colourful streets and over the New Cut. [4]
  • Roads: the A4 Bath Road and the A37 Wells Road meet at Three Lamps, at the edge of Totterdown. [6]
  • Hills: many streets are steep. Vale Street has an average gradient of about 21.8%. [9]

Is Totterdown in the Clean Air Zone?

No. Bristol's Clean Air Zone has been running since 28 November 2022. [10] Totterdown sits just outside it: the boundary starts at the Three Lamps junction, so drivers coming in on the Bath Road can turn onto the Wells Road without entering the zone. [5]

  • Charge: £9 a day for non-compliant private cars; fully electric vehicles don't pay. [10]
  • Possible rise: the council has considered raising some charges to £14 a day. [11] Check the council's checker before you drive in.

What is changing near Totterdown?

  • Residents' parking and Liveable Neighbourhood: both are being consulted on or designed now. Read the guide.
  • Temple Island: Bristol City Council approved Legal & General's £350m Temple Island scheme, with 520 homes, offices, a hotel and shops, in April 2026. [12] Objectors argued the towers would block views of Totterdown's coloured houses from the city. [13]

Community groups

  • TRESA (Totterdown Residents' Environmental and Social Action) holds public meetings on planning, transport and local issues. [14]
  • Arts trail: the Totterdown Arts Trail opens homes to visitors every November.
